housing: The Isle of Wight's private rented stock is spread across its seaside towns and Newport. Many of the large Victorian houses, guest houses and hotels in Ryde, Sandown and Shanklin have been converted into flats and shared homes, and the council notes that the island has many HMOs, as in other seaside areas. Inland and in the West Wight there are stone cottages, bungalows and holiday homes. Private renting grew between 2011 and 2021, and rents rose faster than the South East average in 2026.
checkinTips: Seafront homes in Ryde, Sandown and Shanklin: look for salt corrosion on window frames, balcony rails and door furniture, and damp on exposed walls.
Former guest houses and hotels converted into flats: photograph each flat's door, meters, fire doors, alarms and the shared hallway.
Homes in Ventnor and on the Undercliff: photograph any cracks in walls, sticking doors and garden walls, as the area has known ground movement.
Thatched or stone cottages in the villages: record the roof, chimneys, beams and any damp in thick walls, and the oil tank if there is one.
Homes near the Medina and low-lying harbours: look for signs of past flooding in ground-floor rooms.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact the Isle of Wight Council's housing renewal (private sector housing) team, after first reporting the problem to their landlord.
